The ripple counter, or serial counter, is a basic asynchronous binary counter.
INTRODUCTIONM
Using JK flip-flops in the toggle mode, MODs 2, 4, 8, etc. are available.
Ripple counters can also produce a modified modulus of 3, 5, 10, etc.
DEFINITION

MODIFIED MODULUS - A counter that does not use all of its possible MODs or states. An example is a 3 flip-flop ripple counter which normally is a MOD 8 (2x2x2=8). This counter could be constructed so that it would reset at a lower count.
Ripple counters can also produce a modified modulus of 3, 5, 10, etc...
Using the CLEAR input to the JK flip-flops allows the counter to count to any binary number and reset.

LESSON MENU
A ripple counter is designed to count pulses in binary.....
DISCUSSION
The counter is called ripple because the flip-flop output pulses ripple through the flip-flops.
Notice that the Least Significant Digit is on the left (QA).
In the schematic the most significant digit (QD) is on the right. Remember, when writing and reading binary numbers start at the left with the MSD.
An advantage of a ripple counter is that it operates in various MODs by using the CLEAR input.
With the CLEAR input high, the counter operates normally and counts from 0000 to 1111.
With the CLEAR input high, the counter operates normally and counts from 0000 to 1111.
When the CLEAR input goes low, the counter is reset to 0000. The CLEAR input overrides the input to the clock.
Setting the CLEAR input low at certain counts allows the counter to operate in different MODs.
Connecting the Q or Q outputs to a logic gate controls when the register resets.
Without the logic gate connection this counter will operate as a MOD 16 counter.
MOD 16 counters produce a binary output that can represent
Using the logic gate connection, a MOD16 counter can operate as a MOD 8 counter for octal numbers.
Since the clear input goes low on the eighth count, the counter is a MOD 8.
Connecting the QD output to the NAND gate sends a low to the CLEAR inputs on the eighth count.
The counter starts at 0000. The input to the NAND gate produces a high output. This effectively disables the clear inputs and allows the counter to resume operation beginning at the reset state...
When the count increases by 1, the output of the NAND gate remains high.
The count continues to eight. At the eighth count the input to the NAND gate goes high. The output goes low.
The counter will instantly change from 1000 to 0000 when the CLEAR input goes low.
The counter counts from binary 0000 to 0111. When the count reaches 1000, the counter instantly resets. Therefore, 1000 is not considered a count.
What MOD is needed to have a counter represent decimal numbers?
Decimal numbers range from 0 to 9, or ten counts. The MOD is the number of counts.
